chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: Joining Fletcher at the Grand Terrace after Hawkins leaves for Europe
summary: When his own band broke up Horace joined Fletcher at the Grand Terrace as pianist, bringing Crosby and Roy Eldridge. With Hawkins gone, Fletcher combined Chu Berry's swing and Elmer Williams' tone.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I later joined Fletcher at the Grant Terrace when our band broke up. I joined Fletcher; I took Israel Crosby with me. I took Roy Eldridge with me, and Chu Berry was always there with Fletcher, and we had another tenor saxophonist. He was a great saxophonist. He just died recently -- named Elmer Williams. He had a beautiful tone. This was during the time that Coleman Hawkins decided to accept Jack Hilton's offer in Europe and go to Europe. So Fletcher

had to get a combination of the two -- Chu Berry, who could swing, but didn't have the tone And all that Hawk had, but Elmer Williams had the tone, so he had to get the combination of the two together so he could play his arrangement, because everything Fletcher had was built around Hawkins in his arrangement.

So this is the deal. But this is during the Chicago days too. I was still at Swingland, but I would frequent this place, so finally I joined Fletcher at the Grant Terrace because Fletcher wanted me to play piano, and guess who was our vocalist there?
